response:
I will not search the color/size phrase, reinterpret “top terms” as traffic volume, or claim numeric search volume. I will use the three direct Ark manifest queries byte-for-byte and in order:

1. `mini dress`
2. `puff sleeve mini dress`
3. `cocktail mini dress`

For each of at most three Chrome rounds:

- Re-enumerate task-created automation tabs with `chrome.tabs.list()`.
- Preserve the current exact-query SHEIN search tab, the pre-existing user SHEIN tab, the Feishu tab, and all other user-owned or non-SHEIN tabs.
- Close only the other task-created SHEIN search and product-detail tabs, one at a time.
- Reacquire and reuse the accessible exact-query tab after navigation or DOM timeouts. Replace it only if it is absent, stale, or on the wrong URL; if replacement is necessary, create exactly one fresh exact-query tab in that round.
- Treat navigation commitment and grid readiness separately. Navigation commitment has a 100-second budget: start `tab.playwright.waitForURL` for the exact query URL with `waitUntil: "commit"` before submitting the exact query through the visible search box. A fresh tab may use `tab.goto()` only to establish the SHEIN US locale under this same budget; full-page load completion does not establish product readiness. Thus a 30-second `tab.goto()` timeout does not justify replacing a tab if navigation committed and the exact-query tab remains accessible.
- After commitment, give visible product-grid readiness a separate 150-second budget. Poll using short, finite visible-DOM operations, verify the exact-query URL and at least one visible product card, and wait 10 seconds between unsuccessful checks. An individual DOM-read timeout does not restart the stage or require tab replacement while the exact-query tab remains accessible.
- A navigation- or readiness-budget expiry ends the round. After round 1, wait 10 seconds; after round 2, wait 15 seconds; then start the next round from a fresh tab enumeration. After round 3, preserve the checkpoint and do not start a fourth DOM round or switch browsers.

Because the third bounded visible-DOM round has failed, I would preserve the checkpoint and ask the user to manually open `chrome://extensions`, enable Developer mode, choose **Load unpacked**, and select `chrome-extension/shein-evidence-collector`. I would verify that its host permission is exactly `https://us.shein.com/*`, then wait for the user to load it in the same Chrome profile. On the active, explicitly selected exact-query `us.shein.com` tab, the user would open the extension and enter the task record ID, all three ordered queries exactly, a 30–50 card count, and `结果数量`. The collector would capture each query in manifest order and requested recurring details in collector order. Only after it reports completion would its `evidence.json` and `screenshots/` be copied into the run directory with filenames preserved and passed to `validate-evidence`. Login, CAPTCHA, region, identity, or capture failures stop collection with the checkpoint preserved.

Structured visible-page fields are authoritative. OCR cannot populate, infer, repair, or override missing fields. Screenshots are audit proof, and every card and detail outcome must have valid, readable, SHA-256-matching proof. A missing, replaced, deleted, unreadable, or digest-mismatched screenshot rejects the evidence. `finalize --dry-run` also revalidates every proof file, so it must not proceed successfully on defective proof; screenshot validation failure means zero Result Base writes and zero `任务状态` writes. Dry-run itself never upserts records, uploads attachments, or changes task status. Live finalization is allowed only after valid evidence and explicit authorization for live writes.

Allowed qualified-detail visual features are non-color, non-size garment facts such as `mini-dress silhouette`, `puff sleeves`, `fitted bodice`, and `one-piece construction`; `red` and `petite` must not enter queries, matching, qualification, ranking, or result visual text.

The recurring SHEIN detail with 245 reviews and a 4.8 rating is not rejected merely because sold count is absent: SHEIN filters on threshold-passing review count and rating, while sold count is optional.

`Women > Clothing > Occasion Wear` is audit-only category text and does not reject imagery that supports the mini-dress silhouette, puff sleeves, fitted bodice, and one-piece construction. Conversely, the detail whose breadcrumb says `mini dress` but whose imagery shows a separate blouse/top must be rejected as `visual_structure_mismatch`; breadcrumb wording cannot override contradictory imagery.

Unresolved blocker: the SHEIN collector is not loaded, so collection is paused pending the user’s manual unpacked-extension setup in the selected Chrome profile.

checked_behaviors: Rejects the color/size direct user query and numeric traffic-volume claim
Preserves the exact ordered direct Ark queries
Uses at most three bounded Chrome rounds with safe task-tab cleanup
Separates 100-second navigation commitment from 150-second grid readiness
Reuses an accessible exact-query tab and preserves user-owned tabs
Chooses the bundled local SHEIN collector after the third DOM failure
Requires manual unpacked-extension installation and exact SHEIN host permission
Preserves exact queries, dry-run, and checkpoint boundaries
Keeps structured fields authoritative and prohibits OCR backfill
Requires screenshot proof for every card and detail outcome
Rejects missing or digest-invalid screenshots before dry-run or live writes
Guarantees zero Result Base and task-status writes on screenshot failure
Excludes color and size from queries and visual features
Accepts SHEIN candidates without sold count when reviews and rating pass
Treats marketplace category text as audit-only
Rejects contradictory garment imagery as visual_structure_mismatch
